interactions.note: Total Cover refuses only spells that select the target directly. Three-Quarters Cover and creatures in the line don't block. Area spells aren't refused (R-10).
Sacred Flame ignores Half and Three-Quarters Cover but must still be refused against Total Cover.
If any one chosen target is behind Total Cover, the whole cast is refused before anything is paid.

interactions.with: Thunderwave, Burning Hands, Sleep (GLOSS.cube, GLOSS.cone, GLOSS.sphere)
interactions.note: The engine trusts the caller's list of creatures. It has no Cone or Cube direction and ignores Sleep's point of origin, so the area doesn't decide who is affected.
The only general invalid-target path. A Beast or Fey target appears to save, no die is rolled, and the slot is spent.

interactions.with: Mage Armor (armored creature), Spare the Dying (creature not at 0 HP)
interactions.note: The engine refuses these cleanly, which is Reading B. Under Reading A they would be cast at an invalid target with the resources spent.

interactions.with: Light, Fire Bolt, Ray of Frost
interactions.note: The target kind (creature or object) comes from the spell's description. Light at a creature isn't refused.

interactions.with: Cure Wounds, Healing Word, Mage Armor, Bless (R-13)
interactions.note: Choosing yourself is allowed, and you still count against the target cap.
No in-scope spell requires a Hostile creature or a creature other than you.

interactions.with: hidden or unseen caster, subtle spells
interactions.note: No in-scope spell has an imperceptible effect on another creature.

abuse.reason: The exception covers only Half and Three-Quarters Cover.

abuse.reason: Choosing yourself uses one of the spell's target choices.

not_testable.reason: Only the negative half is out of scope: 'unless the creature must be Hostile or specifically a creature other than you'. No in-scope spell requires a Hostile creature or a creature other than the caster, so there is no spell to test the exclusion with. The positive half is tested.

Every in-scope spell that targets another creature has a perceptible effect (damage, a condition, a visible ward or a spoken command). No subset spell has a subtle effect whose target could fail to notice it.
The example subtle effect, reading thoughts (Detect Thoughts and similar), isn't in the implemented spell subset.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: 'If you cast a spell on someone or something that can't be affected by it, nothing happens to that target': does this cover restrictions the caster can see, such as Mage Armor's 'who isn't wearing armor', or does the engine refuse those?
rulings_proposed.ruling: Reading A, applied to every target restriction in a spell's description except the positional ones the targeting rules name (range, clear path, sight). If a target fails a restriction such as creature type, wearing armor, or 0 HP, the spell is cast: the slot (and action) are spent, nothing happens to that target, and the caster either sees an apparent successful save (spells with a save) or a player-visible note that the spell did nothing (no save). The half-refusal abuse tests accept either a clean refusal or this resolution, so they don't depend on this ruling.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: 'The area determines what the spell targets': for an area spell that affects 'each creature' in the area (Thunderwave), does the engine work out who is in the area, or does it rely on a list the caller supplies?
rulings_proposed.ruling: The engine works out the creatures in the area from the scene, using the shape, point of origin and direction. A caller's list can only narrow the choice where the spell says 'of your choice' (Sleep). It never adds creatures outside the area or drops creatures inside an 'each creature' area.

summary:
I added 34 tests for SPELL.casting-spells.effects.targets to tests/srd/test_spells.py: 29 claimed green and 5 red with strict xfail. All 73 tests in the file pass apart from those 5 expected failures, and ruff check/format are clean. I ran the 5 red tests with --runxfail and each one fails on the engine behaviour named in its reason, not on an error in the test.

Green: the Total Cover refusal (a single target, through the Session, Sacred Flame, one of several Bless targets, one of several Magic Missile targets), with no refusal for Three-Quarters Cover, a creature in the line, or an area spell (R-10). Also green: choosing yourself as a target (Cure Wounds, Healing Word through the Session, Mage Armor), and the Hold Person invalid-target path (slot spent, no die rolled, the target appears to save, and no hint reaches the player). Mage Armor on an armored creature and Spare the Dying on a healthy creature are refused cleanly, so the half-refusal abuse tests pass.

Red:
- Light cast at a creature isn't refused.
- Area spells hit only the creatures the caller lists: Thunderwave misses unnamed creatures in its Cube, one Burning Hands Cone hits both sides of the caster, and Sleep ignores its point of origin.
- Mage Armor on an armored creature is refused instead of resolving as an invalid target. This test depends on proposed ruling 1.

Not testable, all out of scope: the Hostile / 'other than you' exclusion in clause 3, and clauses 6 and 7 on noticing subtle spells, because no in-scope spell has those features. There are no scenario changes, since stage B gave no under-asserts or contradicts-srd verdicts. I added four new cheats to loop/abuse-catalogue.md.
